 For Immediate Release
 Healthy SNAP Food Restriction Demonstration Waiver Takes Effect Nov. 1
 Photo Information 
 Photo courtesy of Montana Department of Commerce. 
 October 22 2026
 Contacts: 
 DPHHS: Jon Ebelt, Communications Director, (406) 444-0936, (406) 461-3757, jebelt@mt.gov 
 HELENA, MT — Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS) Director Charlie Brereton today reminded Montanans that the statewide Healthy SNAP Food Restriction Demonstration Waiver will go into effect on Nov. 1, 2026.
 Approved by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA), the demonstration project tests whether restricting specific low-nutrition, high-sugar items encourages healthier shopping patterns and improves long-term health outcomes among Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participants.
 “Our responsibility is to ensure taxpayer-funded SNAP benefits support access to nutritious food and better health outcomes for Montanans,” Dir. Brereton said. “This demonstration gives us an opportunity to evaluate whether these targeted changes help families make healthier choices while reducing the long-term effects of diet-related chronic disease.” 
 Restricted Items Beginning Nov. 1 
 Beginning Nov. 1, Montana SNAP Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards may no longer be used to purchase products falling into four specific categories:
 Candy: A shelf-stable preparation of sugar, honey, or other nutritive or non-nutritive sweeteners, in combination with chocolate, fruits, nuts, or other ingredients, or flavorings, in the form of bars, drops, or pieces. This includes gelatin-based confections (gummies), licorice, hard candies, and compressed sugar pieces.
 High-Sugar Beverages: Non-alcoholic carbonated or flat beverages sweetened with more than 10 grams of added sugar per eight fluid ounces.
 Energy Drinks: High-caffeine beverages containing more than six milligrams (mg) of caffeine per fluid ounce, or over 140 mg per container, combined with added stimulants such as taurine, guarana, or herbal extracts.
 Shelf-Stable Prepared Desserts: Processed, ready-to-eat, pre-packaged sweet food items intended for immediate consumption with minimal whole-food ingredients.
 What Remains Eligible 
 The waiver does not reduce household monthly benefit amounts, alter general SNAP financial eligibility, or impact core grocery groups. Nutritious food staples—including fresh, frozen, or canned fruits and vegetables, meat, poultry, dairy products, grains, and general pantry staples—remain fully covered.
 The waiver also explicitly allows:
 Baking ingredients, real-fruit snacks with no added sugar, and nut- or fruit-based granolas and trail mixes.
 Plain, naturally flavored, or artificially sweetened zero-sugar carbonated or flat water.
 100% fruit or vegetable juices (and juice blends containing more than 50% juice by volume), meal-replacement beverages, and medical-grade electrolyte replacement beverages.
 Milk, milk alternatives, coffee, tea, protein bars, meal-replacement bars, and store-made bakery items.
 Information for Participants and Retailers 
 At Checkout: Authorized retailers’ point-of-sale systems will automatically identify restricted items at checkout. Participants wishing to purchase restricted items may do so using cash, credit, or debit.
 Retailer Compliance: All SNAP-authorized merchants across Montana, including online retailers, are updating point-of-sale systems prior to Nov. 1. A DPHHS-governed index of restricted Universal Product Codes has been made available to retailers.
 Next Steps for Montanans 
 DPHHS and FNA have created point-of-sale flyers and QR quick-reference cards for merchants across the state to help retail staff assist customers at checkout.
 For more information and program guidelines, visit the Healthy SNAP Food Restriction Demonstration Waiver webpage. ( healthySNAP.mt.gov )
